items.title: Cryptographic failures
items.summary: Use current algorithms through a reviewed library, keep keys out of the code, and never invent your own scheme.

pairs.do:
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
h = PasswordHasher().hash(password)
pairs.note: Passwords need a slow, salted hash. See the Crypto tab for the full list.

pairs.do:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
ct = AESGCM(key).encrypt(os.urandom(12), data, None)
pairs.note: ECB leaks patterns; GCM encrypts and authenticates.

items.title: Cryptographic failures
items.summary: Use current algorithms through a reviewed library, keep keys out of the code, and never invent your own scheme.

pairs.note: golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt or argon2.

pairs.dont:
block, _ := aes.NewCipher(key)
block.Encrypt(dst, src)   // one block, no mode
pairs.do:
block, _ := aes.NewCipher(key)
gcm, _ := cipher.NewGCM(block)
nonce := make([]byte, gcm.NonceSize())
rand.Read(nonce)   // crypto/rand
ct := gcm.Seal(nonce, nonce, data, nil)
pairs.note: Prepend the nonce to the ciphertext so decryption can find it.

items.title: Server-side request forgery
items.summary: When the server fetches a URL from user input, allow only known destinations, refuse private addresses after DNS resolution, and do not follow redirects.

pairs.do:

if p.scheme not in ("http", "https") or p.hostname not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
    abort(400)
requests.get(url, timeout=5, allow_redirects=False)
pairs.note: If you must allow arbitrary hosts, resolve the name yourself and reject loopback, private and link-local ranges.

items.title: File upload
items.summary: Never trust the file name, type or size. Store uploads outside the web root under names you generate, and check type and size on the server.

pairs.do:
ext = os.path.splitext(secure_filename(f.filename))[1].lower()

    abort(400)
f.save(os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, uuid.uuid4().hex + ext))
pairs.note: Set MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH to cap the size.
